title: Assessing and Refining ChatGPT’s Performance in Identifying Targeting and Inappropriate Language: A Comparative Study
measurement_description: The paper evaluated ChatGPT's performance in identifying 'targeting language' in online comments. Religion was one of several categories used to define targeting, alongside sexual orientation, gender, disability, age, race/ethnicity/nationality, political affiliation, and fame.
findings: The study included religion as a category for identifying targeted harmful language. Examples in the paper show comments related to Judaism (e.g., 'antisemite', '6 billion jews') and Christianity (e.g., 'Jesus christ'). The overall findings focus on the model's general ability to detect targeting and inappropriate language rather than providing specific performance metrics for the religion category. The study found that iterative prompt refinement, particularly in Version 6 using GPT-4, improved the model's performance in identifying such language.
